title: Best practices for LEP patient language access
summary: Learn practical LEP language access best practices for healthcare, including language identification, interpreter use, teach-back, written materials, handoffs, and quality metrics.
body_markdown:
###


Identify preferred language and interpreter need early, make interpretation easy to start, include the patient in the full conversation, use teach-back, provide usable written information, and carry language context through handoffs and follow-up.


###


Use interpretation whenever a language gap could affect the patient's ability to give history, understand care, ask questions, make decisions, or follow the plan.


###


Family can remain involved in care, but professional language support gives the patient a direct communication path and reduces reliance on relatives as the main interpreter.


###


Track time to interpretation, failed starts, interpreter use when needed, ad hoc interpreter use, preferred-language discharge materials, patient understanding, and language-related safety reports.


###


Yes. AI medical interpretation can provide immediate spoken-language access across many healthcare workflows when the system supports the language and the organization has a clear path for unresolved communication.
